title: Lesson Plan — Arithmetic Progressions (Class 10 NIOS Mathematics)
subject: Mathematics
objectives: Recognise an arithmetic progression and identify its first term and common difference.
Apply the nth-term formula aₙ = a + (n − 1)d to find any specified term.
Recover (a, d) given any two terms of an AP.
Apply the sum formula Sₙ = n/2 · [2a + (n − 1)d] (or its (a + l) form) to compute partial sums.
Insert one or more arithmetic means between two given numbers.
Translate uniform-step word problems into AP form and solve them.
prerequisites: Basic algebra: linear equations and simple quadratic factoring.
Substitution and simplification with positive and negative numbers.
Familiarity with sequences from earlier classes.
materials: Cards bearing finite sequences for the 'AP-or-not?' sort
Calculator (optional, for the larger sum drills)

activities.description: Quick warm-up. Write three sequences on the board — 5, 9, 13, 17, … ; 10, 7, 4, 1, … ; 1, 4, 9, 16, … — and ask students to predict the next term in each. Point out that two of them follow an 'add a fixed amount' rule and one does not. Introduce the term ARITHMETIC PROGRESSION.

Pair card sort: each pair gets six sequence cards. They must classify each card as AP (and supply a, d) or NOT AP. Mix increasing, decreasing, constant and non-AP cases — including a tricky 1, 3, 6, 10 (triangular numbers).
teacher_actions: Listen for the 'differences must all be equal' rule emerging.
Pick one pair to defend a borderline classification.
student_actions: Compute consecutive differences for each card.
Tag each card AP / NOT AP and write (a, d) for the APs.

activities.description: Direct instruction in four blocks. (i) Definition, common difference, sign of d. (ii) Derive aₙ = a + (n−1)d on the board, with two worked examples — finding a₁₀ and finding n given aₙ. (iii) Derive Sₙ via the pairing trick (first + last paired, n/2 pairs each summing a + l), present both forms. (iv) Arithmetic mean and the 'n means in (n+1) gaps' rule.
teacher_actions: Build aₙ formula by counting the (n−1) jumps from a₁.
Demonstrate the pairing diagram for Sₙ.
Box both formulas at the top of the board for the rest of the lesson.
Call out the 'two-term recovery' technique d = (aₙ − aₘ)/(n − m).
student_actions: Take notes; replicate every worked step.
Verify each example by re-substituting back.
Add the two boxed formulas to a 'rules card' for revision.

activities.description: Worked-problem station. Students do six worksheet items: (1) identify AP and state d, (2) find a₂₀, (3) recover (a, d) from two terms, (4) sum first 30 terms, (5) sum 2 + 4 + 6 + … + 100, (6) word problem (savings or loan).
teacher_actions: Circulate; offer the smallest hint that unblocks each student.
Collect common slips for the Evaluate phase.
Pair fast finishers with peers who need support.
student_actions: Compare answers in pairs after each item.

activities.description: Exit-ticket: 6 quick items, one per outcome. Students complete in 8 minutes; the teacher projects answers and runs a 4-minute discussion of the two items most students missed.
teacher_actions: Distribute exit-ticket; remind it is individual.
Tally; address top two miss items.
student_actions: Self-mark and write a one-line reflection.

activities.description: Set homework: rest of the worksheet; plus one CREATE prompt — 'Construct your own real-world AP problem (loan, salary, stack, savings) and solve it for both the nth term and the sum.' Preview the next chapter (Percentage and Its Applications).

homework: Complete the remaining problems on the Worksheet — Arithmetic Progressions.
Construct your own real-world AP problem (loan, salary, stack or savings) and solve for both the nth term and the partial sum.
Insert 5 arithmetic means between 2 and 26; verify by listing the resulting AP and checking d.
assessment_ideas: Use the 6-item exit ticket as a quick formative check.
Set a 12-question quiz drawn from the chapter bank for the next class as summative.
Mark the LONG_ANSWER on a savings or loan problem using the auto-grade rubric.
Run a 5-minute peer-grading round on the CREATE homework using a two-criterion rubric (correct (a, d)? correct nth term and sum?).
references: NIOS Secondary Mathematics, Module 2, Lesson 7: Arithmetic Progressions.
NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 5: Arithmetic Progressions (parallel CBSE syllabus).
